claims.text: The persistence of a protective oxide on CrFeCoNiX above 900 °C is governed by selective oxidation of X.
In CrFeCoNiSi, selective oxidation of Si forms a continuous, strongly adherent SiO2-rich layer.
In CrFeCoNiAl, selective oxidation of Al forms a continuous, strongly adherent Al2O3-rich layer.
SiO2- or Al2O3-rich layers limit oxygen diffusion and preserve structural integrity.
Oxidation of Mn in CrFeCoNiMn produces a less refractory, discontinuous oxide.
The Mn-derived oxide is prone to cracking and spallation.
Preferential oxidation of Si or Al produces a dense, slow-growing oxide scale.
The Si- or Al-derived oxide scale adheres to the substrate and minimizes further oxygen ingress.
Mn forms comparatively mobile oxides that fail to develop a continuous layer.
Thermal stresses cause the discontinuous Mn-derived scale to crack and spall.
Above 900 °C, CrFeCoNiSi and CrFeCoNiAl will form uniform, adherent, slow-growing oxide films that remain intact.
Above 900 °C, CrFeCoNiMn will form a discontinuous oxide scale prone to cracking and spallation.
The proposed mechanism applies to both single-phase and multiphase CrFeCoNiX metallic solid-solution states.
The proposed mechanism applies in oxidative or corrosive environments above 900 °C.
Microstructural variation and interactions among alloying elements may alter oxide formation and adhesion.
A CrFeCoNi alloy lacking X is an appropriate control for comparing oxide formation behavior.
Protective behavior by CrFeCoNiMn equivalent to that of the Si- or Al-containing alloys would falsify the proposed selective-oxidation mechanism.
Protective behavior by the CrFeCoNi control similar to that of the Si- or Al-containing alloys would falsify the proposed selective-oxidation mechanism.
